nodes.summary: The uniform distribution satisfies detailed balance with the Jukes–Cantor matrix (the matrix is symmetric), hence is stationary.
nodes.title: Detailed balance of the Jukes–Cantor chain

nodes.summary: Kolmogorov forward equation for the Jukes–Cantor model: `d/dt P(t) = P(t) Q` with `Q = jcRate μ`.
nodes.title: Kolmogorov forward equation

nodes.summary: `-(3/4) · log (1 - 4/3 · pDiff μ t i) = μ * t`, the expected number of substitutions per site along the branch.
nodes.title: The Jukes–Cantor distance correction

nodes.summary: The Jukes–Cantor distance: the expected number of substitutions per site corresponding to a proportion `p` of differing sites. Meaningful only for `0 ≤ p < 3/4`; outside that range the value is Lean's totalized logarithm, not a distance (at `p = 3/4` it is `0`).
nodes.title: Jukes–Cantor distance

nodes.summary: The eigenbasis as a unit, with its explicit inverse.
nodes.title: Invertible Jukes–Cantor eigenbasis

nodes.summary: An eigenbasis of the Jukes–Cantor rate matrix, as columns: the constant vector (eigenvalue `0`) and three vectors with zero sum (eigenvalue `-4 μ / 3`).
nodes.title: Eigenbasis of the Jukes–Cantor rate matrix

nodes.summary: `jcProb μ t = exp (t • jcRateMatrix μ)`.
nodes.title: The Jukes–Cantor transition matrix is the matrix exponential of the rate matrix

nodes.summary: The Jukes–Cantor transition probabilities are nonnegative when `0 ≤ μ * t`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of Jukes–Cantor transition probabilities

nodes.summary: At time `0` the Jukes–Cantor transition matrix is the identity.
nodes.title: Jukes–Cantor transition matrix at time zero is the identity

nodes.summary: The Jukes–Cantor transition probability from base `i` to base `j` over a branch of length `t`, with substitution rate `μ`.
nodes.title: Jukes–Cantor transition probability

nodes.summary: The Jukes–Cantor rate matrix as a `Matrix`.
nodes.title: Jukes–Cantor rate matrix as a matrix

nodes.summary: Off-diagonal Jukes–Cantor rates are nonnegative when `0 ≤ μ`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of off-diagonal Jukes–Cantor rates

nodes.summary: The Jukes–Cantor rate matrix: rate `μ / 3` to each other base, `-μ` on the diagonal.
nodes.title: Jukes–Cantor rate matrix

nodes.summary: The Jukes–Cantor transition matrix over a branch with `0 ≤ μ * t`, packaged as a `StochasticMatrix` on the four states `Fin (3 + 1)` so that the finite Markov-chain API (matrix powers, stationarity, detailed balance) applies to it.
nodes.title: Jukes–Cantor transition matrix as a stochastic matrix

nodes.summary: The `n`-step matrix of the Jukes–Cantor chain observed every `t` time units is the transition matrix over the branch length `n * t` (Chapman–Kolmogorov).
nodes.title: Chapman–Kolmogorov equation for the Jukes–Cantor chain

nodes.summary: The probability that the two ends of a branch differ is `3/4 · (1 - exp (-4 μ t / 3))`, whatever the starting base.
nodes.title: Closed form of the Jukes–Cantor difference probability

nodes.summary: The probability that the ends of a branch differ is below the saturation value `3/4`, for all real `μ` and `t` (it is negative when `μ * t < 0`, see `pDiff_mem_Ico`).
nodes.title: Jukes–Cantor difference probability is below 3/4

nodes.summary: For `0 ≤ μ * t` the probability that the ends of a branch differ lies in `[0, 3/4)`, the domain of `jcDistance`.
nodes.title: Jukes–Cantor difference probability lies in (0, 3/4)

nodes.summary: The probability that the ends of a branch differ is nonnegative when `0 ≤ μ * t`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the Jukes–Cantor difference probability

nodes.summary: The probability that the two ends of a branch of length `t` carry different bases, given base `i` at the start.
nodes.title: Probability that the ends of a branch differ

nodes.summary: Diagonalization of `t • jcRateMatrix μ`.
nodes.title: Diagonalization of the Jukes–Cantor rate matrix

nodes.summary: Chapman–Kolmogorov equation for the Jukes–Cantor model.
nodes.title: Chapman–Kolmogorov equation

nodes.summary: The right-hand side of the forward equation, in closed form.
nodes.title: Right-hand side of the Jukes–Cantor forward equation in closed form

nodes.summary: Each row of the Jukes–Cantor transition matrix sums to `1`.
nodes.title: Rows of the Jukes–Cantor transition matrix sum to one

nodes.summary: Each row of the Jukes–Cantor rate matrix sums to `0`.
nodes.title: Rows of the Jukes–Cantor rate matrix sum to zero

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
